Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 1. Platform Overview

PrimeInspect is an inspection and audit management platform built by Tecsack Software. It

gives organizations a configurable way to define inspection templates, schedule them across

sites and equipment, assign them to field users, and capture the results — including photo,

video, and signature evidence — through to a finished report.

The platform is industry-agnostic by design: the type of equipment being inspected, the checklist

content, and the inspection frequency are all configured per customer account rather than being

built for one specific industry. This makes it suitable for facilities management, equipment

maintenance, and safety or compliance auditing programs alike.

PrimeInspect is delivered as a backend API platform (ASP.NET Web API on .NET 9) that

powers mobile and web client applications used by administrators and field inspection teams.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. Workflow

At a high level, an administrator builds a reusable inspection template, schedules it against the

relevant sites and assets, and field users complete it on location. Findings that fail or are

flagged during an inspection can be escalated into a tracked follow-up ticket.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. Workflow > 2.1 Inspection Setup

The Inspection Setup stage defines what gets inspected and how.

· Inspection Forms:Reusable templates made upof one or more sections, built by an

administrator.

· Sections:Named groupings of checklist itemswithin a form (e.g., a section per area or

system).

· Checklist Items:Individual questions or taskswithin a section. Each item can be

configured to require a photo, video, written note, and/or signature as evidence.

· Object Types:Account-defined categories usedto classify the assets being inspected

(for example, an HVAC unit or a fire extinguisher).

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. Workflow > 2.2 Scheduling & Assignment

Once a template exists, it is put on a schedule and turned into work for field teams.

●
Scheduler:Administrators define how often aninspection form should run.

●
Job Generation:A background service periodicallychecks due schedules and

generates concrete Inspection Jobs from them.

●
Assignment:Jobs are assigned to specific users,sites, and assets; field users see

their assigned work through a mobile dashboard.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. Workflow > 2.3 Field Execution & Reporting

Field users complete assigned jobs and the results are turned into a shareable report.

· Inspection Data:Field users work through eachchecklist item and record the result,

attaching photos, video, notes, or a signature as required.

· Evidence Capture:Photos and files are uploadeddirectly to secure cloud storage rather

than passing through the API server itself.

· PDF Reports:A completed inspection can beexported as a PDF report.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. Workflow > 2.4 Service Requests

When a checklist item is flagged or fails during an inspection, it can generate a Service Request

— a follow-up ticket carrying a priority and due date, assigned to a responsible user, and linked

back to the inspection job that raised it. This lets issues found in the field be tracked through to

resolution rather than only recorded in a report.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. Workflow > 2.5 Organizations, Sites & Assets

Inspection activity is organized around a simple structure:

Account:The billing and tenant boundary; inspectiondata is scoped to an account.

●
Organization:A customer's own internal structure,such as departments or branches.

●
Sites:Physical locations belonging to an account.

●
Assets:The individual pieces of equipment orobjects being inspected at a site.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. Workflow > 2.6 Access & Plans

· Roles & Permissions:Each role is granted specificread/write access to individual

platform features, and access is enforced on every request.

· Subscription Plans:Free and paid subscriptiontiers apply configurable limits — such

as the number of inspection templates or the volume of inspections — which are enforced

automatically.

· Notifications:Users receive in-app notificationsto keep them informed of assigned jobs

and account activity.

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 2. Workflow > 2.7 Overall Platform Journey

The primary workflow, end to end:

Build Template → Schedule & Assign → Execute & Capture Evidence → Report / Flag

Issues → Resolve via Service Request

Section: COMPANY PROFILE > 4. Sourcing Notes

This overview was compiled by reviewing the application's underlying source code — its

controllers, services, and data model — rather than from a separate written specification. It

reflects how the platform currently behaves as of this review, and is intended as a functional

reference rather than a design document.

A few points are worth keeping in mind when relying on this profile:

●
Authorization checks: Authorization is currentlydisabled on several endpoints

(including organization, service request, checklist-data, account, and record endpoints),

so these can be reached without a valid session. Worth reviewing before wider release,

given this document's classification.

●
Placeholder endpoints: Two API areas (attachmentmanagement and a general

person lookup) exist in the API surface but currently return placeholder responses rather

than being implemented. Actual file uploads are handled through a separate, working

attachment-data endpoint.

●
Location tracking: GPS coordinate/event trackingexists in the data model but

appears to be an early-stage, largely unfinished feature.

●
Plan limit enforcement: A per-inspection usage limitfor subscription plans is

implemented in code but is not currently active.

●
Environment configuration: The application currentlypoints to development

database and service settings rather than a distinct production configuration.

●
Background jobs: The background Windows Servicethat generates inspection jobs

and processes outbound email is currently set to always run its full job list rather than on

its intended timer-based schedule.
